svg.title: What the search returned, and why
svg.desc: The fourteen stored facts, sorted by the cosine similarity of their sentence to the question, between 0.54 and 0.74, with a line at the 0.6 floor. The search returns ten: facts that share a word with the question, and facts above the floor, merged. Returned: the dinner plan, stored twice (0.739), Indian cuisine (0.665), the budget (0.658), the assistant's note that fish is in (0.658), the sister named Lena (0.653), Lena cannot eat shellfish (0.636), the closed vegetarian fact (0.608, tenth), paneer dishes (0.608), and Lena and Jonas as a couple (0.599, under the floor but returned for its shared words). Not returned: the peanut allergy (0.602, over the floor but eleventh), Jonas's coeliac disease (0.596), the pescatarian fact that replaced the vegetarian one (0.592) and the move to Kreuzberg (0.542).
svg.text: What the search returned, and why
Every stored fact, scored by how close its sentence is in meaning to the question. All fourteen fall in a narrow band, and
the floor of 0.6 cuts through it. The search keeps ten: facts that share a word with the question, and facts over the floor,
the same dinner sentence, second edge
the assistant: fish is now included
Lena and Jonas are a couple
The floor decides at the third decimal.
The closed fact is in at 0.608; the fact that replaced it is out at 0.592; Jonas's coeliac disease is out at 0.596.
A shared word gets a fact in anyway.
“Lena and Jonas are a couple” is under the floor and comes second, for the words it shares with the question.
The peanut allergy passes the floor and comes eleventh. The closed fact took the tenth place, and the dinner sentence stored twice took two.
Bold rows are the four facts the answer needs.
